close_alternatives.reason: 013 tests whether a local allocation relation can justify an action without ranking complete lives and gives a distributive case. 077’s eventual-sign relation is precise, but its horizon-neutrality premise is still unsupported and the closest literature is likely very near.

Both concern a system changing the terms of assessment. 059 supplies a concrete self-validating reform test—whether relevant objections remain usable. 103 may reduce directly to construct validity/treatment versions and requires a more elaborate estimand argument before a distinct contribution is shown.

080 isolates a person-specific wrong and a currently endorsed authoritative exclusion, with a remedy-content countertest. 119’s custody role identifies a real access act, but its reparative status may add no content beyond stewardship or aid.

111 preserves the unusual-route requirement with a defined role test, a computable leakage question, and explicit rights-based defeaters. 051’s proposed value difference is unsettled if temporal phenomenology is fully matched and may instead be authenticity or agency.

Both concern authority after communication or personal change. 007 presents a sharper claim-object/bearer distinction under branching and explicit burden tests; 005’s notice rule is narrower and may be absorbed by familiar consent and revocation doctrine.

115 separates psychological connection, welfare-bearer identity, and permission to impose harm, with a sign-reversal probe. 056’s result depends on an unearned communicative-desert premise and a difficult fairness procedure for public answerability.

deferral_reasons.idea-003: The pause right is sharply limited by a pre-existing charter, neutral decision-maker, and deadline. That may make it an application of established governance or ex ante fairness rather than a distinct disclosure-timing contribution; the six probe slots go to candidates with more discriminating argument tests.
deferral_reasons.idea-005: The opportunity-without-acknowledgment rule is clear, but it is confined to unilateral revocation and may be fully covered by familiar consent, notice, and authority rules. It also overlaps the broader authority-and-uptake problem in idea-007; its nearest source distinction is less developed here.
deferral_reasons.idea-022: The proposal correctly denies that intervention boundaries identify subjects, but its positive output is a report across independently supplied welfare partitions. Without a defended bridge or decision rule, this is presently more a diagnostic framework than a settled argument; the source and engineering-versus-subject tests remain wide.
deferral_reasons.idea-026: Strict set inclusion gives a clean local comparison only after an independently justified task profile is fixed. The core formal property is straightforward, while the difficult normative premise risks moving the same master standard into the task profile; idea-013 has a more direct action-level claim and distributive case.
deferral_reasons.idea-028: The worked post-draw exception changes A’s probability from one half to five eighths, so the current example can be explained by unequal outcomes. The proposal itself admits it has not isolated a procedural complaint under guaranteed equal chances; that key case should exist before it earns a probe slot.
deferral_reasons.idea-031: The affirmative argument applies only to a temporally responsive agent under an accepted invitation norm and does not establish the theological application. Timelessness and divine goodness are not bridged by the human example, leaving a very broad source burden for a narrow conditional result.
deferral_reasons.idea-043: The proposal expressly treats its result as a role-specific application of responsible assurance, not an established irreducible duty. Its trigger and remedy overlap familiar dependency repair, trust, and stewardship; idea-111 offers a more discriminating test between a role duty and general aid.
deferral_reasons.idea-051: The central experiential difference remains unstable: if complete temporal phenomenology is matched, the proposal has not established an experiential-value difference; if it is not matched, the cases differ in experience. The author’s falsification conditions are strong, but the actual value-bearing arc is not yet sufficiently specified.
deferral_reasons.idea-056: The thesis depends on a particular communicative account of desert and a fair public measure of completed answerability; if desert is fixed by the culpable act, the result is mercy or mitigation. Its own expansion concedes that the central premise is unearned, and six slots favor candidates with more discriminating tests.
deferral_reasons.idea-057: The loss appears only when an institution assigns a default role or treats silence as authorization. Where a neutral exit restores the prior procedure, the proposal concedes no loss; where exit is blocked, the issue may be an imposed burden or invalid consent rather than a distinct freedom.
deferral_reasons.idea-062: The distinction between moral avowal and accountability undertaking may leave only a promise or repair offer, especially for global error theory; the recipient may reasonably reject it as an apology. It is close to the speech-act and normative-authority questions in other proposals but has no source work yet to show a distinct surviving contribution.
deferral_reasons.idea-067: The policy objection may either be included in a complete outcome description or reduce to expected misuse, correlation, fear, or lost options. The author carefully exposes this dispute, but the residual standing premise is not yet separated from established non-domination accounts.
deferral_reasons.idea-077: The eventual-sign relation is mathematically explicit, but the ethical premise that all cofinal horizons are equally admissible remains unsupported and may simply encode incompleteness. The proposal also points directly to established overtaking/asymptotic-dominance literature; idea-013 is preferred for the current formal slot because it has a concrete institutional allocation case.
deferral_reasons.idea-085: The argument is conditional on deliberate public authorization, no later revocation, no delegation, and a status-asserting editorial label. Under those stipulations the distinction between preference and authority is intelligible, but it may be a direct application of established intentionalism and edition practice; the six selected directions have broader philosophical stakes.
deferral_reasons.idea-088: The author concedes that correction infrastructure cannot improve evidence-level warrant. The remaining possibility is an all-things-considered or practice-level permission whose epistemic classification is expressly unresolved; this leaves a less determinate positive claim than the selected candidates.
deferral_reasons.idea-092: The distinction among closure time, deadline evaluation, and duty violation is careful, but the central claim is narrow and may be a clarification of the fixed semantics of “by the deadline.” The task-identity problem under cancellation remains open, and the probe funnel prioritizes claims with broader payoff.
deferral_reasons.idea-103: The package-effect/kind-specific distinction is important, but the expansion itself identifies construct validity, treatment versions, and estimand specification as close alternatives and does not yet show a distinct inference. It also requires a complex formal estimand account; the selected directions offer more discriminating near-term probes.
deferral_reasons.idea-119: The custodian’s distinct action—preserve and arrange access—is clear, but its special reparative classification may add no content beyond ordinary stewardship or role-based aid. It is close to idea-080’s institutional repair but has a less direct person-specific wrong and remains dependent on the contested “reparative” label.

idea-007.contribution: A promise may remain one recipient-directed claim after personal branching while qualifying successors bear only bounded, alternative responsibility for securing that one performance.
idea-007.hardest_objection: The successors may be numerically distinct, nonconsenting agents; the proposed burden cap and successor threshold may fail to justify assigning them any duty.
idea-007.probe_can_settle: Compare primary accounts of fission, promissory claim-rights, and responsibility transfer; test whether they support any successor duty without treating memory as identity, and run forced-branching, divided-control, and one-successor-can-perform cases.
idea-007.why_probe: The expansion states a precise single-claim/divided-responsibility distinction and gives a genuine failure condition. The unresolved burden is philosophically substantive and can be tested against close primary theories.

idea-013.contribution: A justified choice among feasible interventions need not entail a complete ranking of recipients’ whole lives when the relevant action reasons form a coherent incomplete relation and any tie procedure is independently defended.
idea-013.hardest_objection: The local intervention relation and its distributive context may simply hide a complete ordering, or may leave the allocator unable to justify a required choice.
idea-013.probe_can_settle: Reconstruct primary accounts of incomplete social orderings and person-affecting allocation; check a finite graph for cycles, maximal elements, and tie cases, then test whether the argument adds anything beyond an established action-relative decision procedure.
idea-013.why_probe: It offers an explicit formal claim and a worked distribution-sensitive example, while exposing rather than concealing the substantive priority premises. A bounded formal and source probe can distinguish the mathematical point from the philosophical conclusion.

idea-059.contribution: When deliberative improvement is part of a reform’s justification, silence or agreement is weak evidence of success if affected participants lack a usable way to state and receive an answer to relevant objections.
idea-059.hardest_objection: The condition may preserve harmful old concepts or impose an unbounded duty to translate every objection, while familiar deliberative and conceptual-engineering theories may already supply it.
idea-059.probe_can_settle: Read closest primary accounts of conceptual engineering, metalinguistic negotiation, and deliberative contestation; apply the proposal’s usable-route test to cases where a concept changes but a concrete objection is translated into the new vocabulary.
idea-059.why_probe: The proposal gives a practical adequacy test and a counterexample in which complaint counts fall because the system no longer records objections. A source comparison can determine whether this is a distinct epistemic constraint or an application of familiar contestability requirements.

idea-080.contribution: An institution that still endorses an authoritative, wrongful exclusion may owe a person-specific retraction after the excluded person’s death, even where no later welfare or benefit to living people is stipulated.
idea-080.hardest_objection: Truthfulness or institutional integrity may fully explain the retraction, leaving no surviving directed claim owed to the deceased; the remedial claim may not outlast its bearer.
idea-080.probe_can_settle: Compare primary accounts of posthumous rights and directed duties, corrective/reparative justice, and institutional agency; test endorsed exclusion against a neutral record error and an already-retracted historical verdict while holding living effects fixed.
idea-080.why_probe: The candidate identifies a current institutional act—continued endorsement—and a remedy-content test, rather than relying only on posthumous welfare. It is worth probing because the key distinction has concrete countercases and can be rejected if integrity fully absorbs it.

idea-111.contribution: A co-maintainer of an optional disclosure practice may owe proportionate protection against a predictable refusal signal, with truthful cover refusal as a last resort when redesign is unavailable and the privacy interest is legitimate.
idea-111.hardest_objection: The proposed special duty may reduce to ordinary easy aid; asking non-exempt participants to withhold truthful information may burden autonomy, mislead observers, or move rather than reduce the privacy risk.
idea-111.probe_can_settle: Read primary work on privacy, inference, group disclosure, role responsibility, and duties of aid; model what observers infer under cover and side information; compare organizer, routine participant, and bystander cases with equal cost and capacity.
idea-111.why_probe: This preserves the campaign’s reserved unusual route because the claim is conditional, has a clear role-removal test, and treats cover as defeasible rather than automatic. Its novelty and even its distinct role-duty basis are unknown, so it must face a serious attempt at defeat.

idea-115.contribution: Weak psychological continuity may limit a stage’s future-directed stake without by itself deciding which experiences belong to one welfare-bearing life or whether later pleasure compensates for earlier suffering.
idea-115.hardest_objection: A theory may coherently use different grounds for stage-relative interests, welfare-bearer identity, and aggregation; the proposal could therefore expose only terminology, not an inconsistency.
idea-115.probe_can_settle: Reconstruct a close primary theory of time-relative interests and temporal welfare; apply its own rules to the proposed case and a sign-reversed case, separating stage interest, life-level welfare, and permission to impose harm.
idea-115.why_probe: The expansion retreats from a blanket inconsistency charge and identifies a falsifiable calibration question. A probe can test whether its selected target already provides independent, nonselective grounds or whether cross-temporal compensation is being asserted without a bridge.

decision.comparability: Selection follows the fixed order, not an ordinal ranking or score sum. The requested gpt-6-luna/xhigh setting is not backend verification. All six novelty claims remain unknown or bounded; no competition winner or midterm result is inferred.

idea-007.reason: The probe rejects automatic or divided inheritance of a promise by nonconsenting successors. The surviving case is a successor’s explicit fresh assurance or joint uptake, which may be ordinary promissory theory rather than a distinct fission contribution. The transfer question, fair burden rule, and central directedness bridge remain unresolved on the bounded sources. A new essay centered on promise-directedness would also sit close to already accepted promise-focused work; no distinct advance over that portfolio is clear at this point.

idea-080.reason: The probe does not establish a person-directed remedial claim persisting after death. Its defensible remainder is a current institutional duty to withdraw an unjustified authoritative status for reasons of truth and institutional integrity. That is a plausible narrower topic, but it substantially overlaps the existing correction essay’s institutional remedial subject, while the distinctive posthumous claim failed its key test. Do not count a relabeled version as a separate essay.

idea-115.reason: The assigned Wendler article directly covers same-individual temporal compensation, psychological connection, whole-life comparison, and an independent limit on severe suffering; Harman supplies a related near/far challenge. The probe found no specified target theory with the proposed inconsistency and no distinct surviving test. Novelty is unknown, and the bounded record does not support advancing this as a standalone essay.

decision.method: Each direction receives a fresh isolated English full author, exact primary-source search and saved source coverage before draft, a fresh separate manuscript critic, and reasoned same-author revision. Preserve failed paths and limitations. Do not force acceptance of a materially defective manuscript.
decision.not_authorized: Midterm, publication, submission, outreach, paid API, quota scheduler, or Claude.
decision.portfolio_deconfliction: Root-only limited title/abstract/opening-section check. It identifies close topic relations but does not prove portfolio-wide non-duplication. Earlier essays and the root comparison are excluded from all new author and critic packets.

reserved_unusual_route.basis: The exact finite test distinguishes a narrow symmetric privacy benefit from material failure under repeated, correlated, nonuniform, or side-informed settings. The redesign-first claim has concrete defeaters and remains contestable; no special-duty or novelty finding is asserted.

idea-013.thesis: A justified selection among feasible interventions need not entail a complete ranking of the recipients’ whole lives, provided the substantive action reasons are independently justified and form an acyclic relation. A unique maximal option can be selected without asserting a whole-life comparison; multiple maxima require a separately justified tie procedure or an admission of underdetermination.
idea-013.why: The probe preserved a precise logical distinction and tested its limits with an exact finite model. It openly concedes that the clinic rule is stipulated, not morally derived, and that the result applies only when the action relation is coherent. A full essay can defend the narrow non-entailment point, develop a more concrete distributive case, and test whether practical allocation reasons quietly encode whole-life rankings.

idea-059.thesis: When a reform’s defenders cite agreement, silence, or fewer objections as evidence that the reform improved deliberation, that evidence is weakened if they know that reasonably foreseeable, relevant objections could not be stated in a form the process would recognize and answer.
idea-059.why: The probe separates the evidential claim from a veto or a general rule against conceptual reform. Its surviving point is limited but useful: a process cannot use the objections it made unavailable as straightforward evidence of deliberative success. The source comparison identified close work on epistemic injustice, concept choice, disagreement, and democratic inclusion; a full essay can determine whether a defensible application survives those precedents.

idea-111.thesis: A person who knowingly accepts responsibility for designing or administering an optional-disclosure procedure, represents or invites reliance on protection for legitimate confidential exceptions, and can foresee that ordinary response patterns will identify an exception has a defeasible reason to assess the leakage and prefer a feasible, minimally restrictive redesign.
idea-111.why: The source-grounded probe rejects a presumed duty to provide a cover refusal but preserves a conditional redesign-first argument. It supplies an exact Bayesian test: random cover can reduce identification under a symmetric toy threat model, while correlation, repetition, side information, and unequal response propensities can increase risk or shift suspicion. This is the campaign’s reserved unusual route, retained because the narrowed governance claim remains arguable and has clear defeat conditions; neither its special-duty basis nor its novelty is established.
